summary:
# NOTES: THE ISLE OF LIES (M. P. Shiel; Gutenberg #77484)

Single book, no BOOK headings. Chapters I–XV. Narrated in shifting first-person documents: Prof. S. S. Reid's diary (ch. I, II), Dr. Lepsius's letters (III, IV), Jeanne Auvache's journal (V–IX), Saïd Pasha's Paris Notes and third-person narration (X–XV).

## Front matter
Publisher: T. Werner Laurie, Clifford's Inn, London. Epigraph: "The sounding again of the mountains." (Ezekiel). Other Shiel works listed: "The White Wedding," "The Last Miracle."

## CH I: THE STELE
- Reid's diary. 1868: Napier takes Magdala; British mission to Abyssinia. Dr. Lepsius (about 45, bachelor, rich, "Jack of all trades"; short, bold nose, thin lips, straight burning hair) goes to Abyssinia, citing Jurassic limestones and Bible MSS.
- Debra-Seena museum on island in Lake Sana. Mission reaches Gondar end of August; Lepsius goes to Lake Sana in September with one Choan servant.
- Monastery island (double monastery) and library/mosque island half a mile away. Prior has died; monks electing successor.
- Two monks: milder one and a grimmer one carrying two falchions in scarlet-morocco scabbards. Galla warrior (giant, shield garnished with human hair) guards coffin.
- Room of the dead prior: basalt stele, thick as a wrist, ~6 inches, copper cap, banyan string, hung under a picture of the Virgin. Labelled "Riches of Jerusalem." Prior spent 50 years on it, died before it. Stele "fell from heaven." To be buried with prior at 11 p.m. in monastery.
- Lepsius at 10 p.m. sneaks out, steals in dark, paddles to library island; waits on rock. Torches are quenched by rain. Coffin loaded into boat; Lepsius hangs from transom. Cuts banyan cords, slides fingers in, begins drawing stele from dead neck. Prior's arm gives way; coffin tilts and sinks. Lepsius (cannot swim well) grabs coffin-lid, still holding stele on string.
- Flight: monks, new prior, fierce monk, huge black fellow chase; abbey-bells ring. Lepsius slashes cocoanut-matting with razor; runs into nunnery full of women; a floor-bed catches fire. Nuns' yowl. He escapes by boat; Ethiopic chiefs (dejamatshs) surround islet; he slips through; hides in forest.
- Morning: British mission at Gondar barricaded; three Abyssinians shot. Lepsius rejoins mission six days later; leaves on sixteenth morning under ras's escort.

## CH II: MOLLY O'HARA
- Reid: Lepsius shows stele; says it is an Indian-incident record, dated no earlier than 13th c.; Coptic-Memphitic mix. Lepsius goes to Galway castle, ill.
- Ten months later: "Just failed"; 15 signs unread, three secret words. Lepsius says he will "make a man who will read the secret."
- Westminster Bridge, July sun, two hours. Lepsius picks out an Irish washerwoman, black hair, black eyes, ~25: **Molly O'Hara** (sister a fruit-seller at Ballihooly). They tour Tower, Crown Jewels, St Paul's whispering-gallery, Chamber of Horrors, play.
- Lepsius: "I mean to marry her." Theory: environment makes man; child isolated in false environment of gods will become god. "Son of Adam never educated."
- Marriage 13 Sept 1869, church at Lambeth. Galway castle. Lepsius leases island of **Shunter** (Outer Hebrides). Son born; Molly dies of milk-fever five days later. Son to be named **Hannibal**.

## CH III: THE ISLE OF LIES
- Lepsius letters. He and **Shan Healy** (servant; "The Idiot") at Barra. Lepsius has head bandaged. Describes Hannibal: middle-sized, swarthy, bluish-black stubble, cruel smile, wild dark eyes "like rupicapra gazelle."
- Birthday 21 July; Hannibal 19; Lepsius 64. Daily race: Hannibal runs west shore, Lepsius east through "tunnel" gorge; Lepsius always wins; Hannibal never. Flag-staff goal to north of island, two miles.
- Eve of birthday: Shan's glass pot boils over; Hannibal throws Shan aside, rushes in. Later Hannibal beats Shan's head on kitchen floor, smiling. Lepsius locked out.
- Night: Hannibal in observatory; complains moon is wrong; Lepsius quotes Genesis "two great lights." Hannibal compares moon to Shan's gum-boil face. Lepsius touches Hannibal's neck, says "Boy"; Hannibal gives "Arctic-cold" gaze.
- Lepsius's backstory: Hannibal's library of purged books cost over £14,000; taught "Peter Pitt" as discoverer of mathematics; no knowledge that Caesar was assassinated or Napoleon defeated; told he was "idiot" Shan; believes Lepsius can shoot, swim, run, etc. Hannibal uses dynamite bombs; learns languages in weeks; "forgetting" unknown to him.

## CH IV: THE SHIP
- Birthday breakfast: Hannibal says he worked at 4:55; age 6,931 days. Lepsius shows stele. Hannibal reads it aloud: "graved on a golden brick within the grave of Arunzebe... eighty princes... white strangers from over the Great Hill... Silence that annihilates. Let no man strive to visit them at—" Three words unread.
- Hannibal asks for half an hour on shore. Gone four days ago; Lepsius waits two hours. Schooner seen to east. Shan finds lady's handkerchief marked "R. V." with stale perfume on western shore. Boat on north harbour empty of two pairs of wagtails; sandal-like footprints on east promontory into sea. Shan finds half a bitten chocolate bon-bon in kelp.
- Lepsius laments, "God only knows" the young man's fate.

## CH V: "MISS EVE."
- Jeanne Auvache (French maid of Miss Eve), journal. Yacht lands on Shunter; party: Miss Ruth (saintly, 25) and Miss Eve Vickery, Lord Astor, Miss Savage, Comte de Courcy (Monsieur le Comte; later Minister of the Interior), Mr. Richard Vickery (father, Bible-reader; "Iron King"; stays aboard).
- Jeanne sees glowing dark eyes in bush; party jokes about "genius of the place," Hermes, Lamia.
- Evening, 8:30, Jeanne's cabin dark; attacked by Hannibal (who swam aboard). He gags her with apron; she switches light on. He says he knows she is a woman and wants her as wife; she nods yes. He makes her vow not to betray him "to Man." Shows her a stone like an ink-bottle: "Read that." She cannot.
- Jeanne called by Miss Eve; Hannibal whispers "Sweet voice."

## CH VI: THE TOWERS
- Landing: Hannibal carries Eve's trunk; boards train with Jeanne. Hannibal trembles, fears "Man" and father. Asks why trains are small; speaks French of Bordeaux.
- Arrive Thring at dawn; The Towers (Vickery home). Jeanne plans marriage: £200 savings, licence from surrogate; hides him in church steeple near St. Peter. He chooses to stay in river-cave; meeting at east shrubbery 9 p.m.

## CH VII: THE TERRACES
- Comte de Courcy proposes to Eve in small drawing-room; she is noncommittal.
- Ball. Jeanne late to shrubbery; Hannibal at window peeping, speaks with Miss Ruth. Ruth asks: ignorant of Jesus Christ? Year "600,363" (from ape-state). Ruth: "He was man and God." Eve: "Why, yes." Hannibal: "Perfect it is, though a Heart not a Head..." (Eve's words). Hannibal says he likes Miss Ruth best, then Jeanne.
- Jeanne tells him Ruth will betray him; he doubts. He listens with ear to ground.

## CH VIII: IN THE GARDEN
- Shan Healy arrives at The Towers seeking master's son. Ruth, promising silence, decides to betray Hannibal (tells Healy to meet him on terraces). Eve: "Promises can't be repealed."
- Jeanne visits cave: finds telescope-like oak, bird-trap, boiling stone vase, "stele."
- Jeanne gets vitriol at Wynton (dated 27th); ordered marriage licence from St. Arvens (Mr. Rae, £2 3s. 6d.); wedding-ring.
- Moonlight: Hannibal reports London grocer George Perkins burned at Up Brooming (rescue attempt). Hannibal calls him thief. Hannibal's conversation with Eve in garden; Hannibal kneels, Eve tells him to leave. Monsieur de Courcy with cane chases him. Hannibal floors the Minister with a blow; cigarette in nostril.
- Night: Jeanne tells Eve of coming marriage; Eve showers Jeanne with gowns (~£1000 worth).

## CH IX: "VITRIOLISERAI."
- Hannibal absent from cave; Jeanne's diary: Healy at Mrs. Bream's cottage; Hannibal and Healy took 10:20 train to London; London chase (Tottenham Court Road; Waterloo Bridge; "idiots"); Hannibal filliped a constable.
- The 26th: police "inspector." The 27th: Jeanne buys vial of vitriol at Wynton. Marriage notice given.
- The 29th: Hannibal returns at night to housekeeper's room with Healy. Asks light; studies the stele with magnifying-glass. Police Inspector Gibbon and Constable Shooter arrive; Hannibal escapes by vitriol-dipped match cutting shirt sleeves; ropes both policemen to old oak tree. Hannibal removes £400 stolen in London.
- Hannibal gives Jeanne vitriol, takes her ninety pounds, leaves note: "Beldam Eve, farewell for two years, from your slave for ever, Hannibal Lepsius. Please tell Jeanne Auvache where I have laid her money." Money found replaced by tissue-paper; half-sovereign on chain.
- 30th: Jeanne vows to vitriolise him. 31st: Eve embraces Jeanne. 2nd: Jeanne plans to leave.

## CH X: "THE MOON."
- Paris, Club des Décavés, Avenue du Bois, June. Duc de Rey-Drouilhet, Abbé Sauriau (Jesuit, shifting red sock), Isabeau Thiéry (poet-politician), Prefect Leflô, Saïd Pasha (Notes), Mr. E. Reader Meade (Englishman).
- Lepsius kissed Eve (Miss Vickery) at Quai d'Orsay soirée; Eve kissed him, per Pasha. Lepsius's Moon scheme: "Moon Company"; stock; Debentures; Exhibition; coup d'état; "steerable bullet."
- Lepsius rides phaeton with American girl secretary. Comte de Courcy's partial letter about world redistribution, Quebec capital.
- Plans: Sixth Correctional Tribunal; oubliettes; "twelve to fifteen years" in bastille on coast.
- Comte de Courcy with Minister: Eve; Jeanne Auvache threw vitriol at Lepsius at Dover (imprisoned five months); Nundcumar (Hindoo servant; cook at Egmond; once ex-convict) to place Jeanne in Lepsius's service.

## CH XI: THE CHAMBER-WINDOW
- Versailles, Villa des Medicis (Comtesse de Pichegru-Picard; Madame Lina Grammont). Healy reports telephone whispering-gallery spying. Healy and Ruth talk; Eve's engagement to de Courcy; Lepsius's note: "I, a suitor for your daughter's hand... Miss Eve Vickery... LEPSIUS."
- Telephone: "Will you have me for a son-in-law?" Eve hisses "I am affianced..."
- Night: Lepsius climbs to Eve's window; she plays Mendelssohn Andante; he barricades room with wardrobe, couch, chair. Long talk on love, evolution, "Genius-of-the-species," "Christ." Eve: "Lepsius, you are full of apes." He leaves via window.
- Lepsius, in Serapis palace, shoots Nundcumar's and then Jeanne's: vitriol to Nundcumar's nose; Jeanne shot in both wrists and feet.

## CH XII: THE WEDDING-PLACE
- Wedding first set 23 July, moved to 5 July; Grönland (Comtesse's Orleans seat) burned. Nundcumar and Healy discuss; Nundcumar's taunts.
- Lepsius speaks with Mr. Meade (Reader Meade); Meade: Egmond château (League lease; Piscari); Schuré (engineer, moon-machine). Lepsius bribes Duc de Rey-Drouilhet, 20,000 francs cheque. Plot: Egmond, arrest in summer-house, transfer to Château Labîme, Ile de Bas.
- Lepsius visits Abbé Sauriau; sends Monsieur Brisson (fake). Abbé with Comte de Courcy: marriage at Egmond.

## CH XIII: AT EGMOND
- Assembly at Egmond. Captain Pertius. Monsieur Brisson of Rouen (limping, bow-legged; fake) hides bombs. Eve meets Lepsius at mosque; Lepsius tells Eve father is with enemies.
- Brisson (fake) kisses Eve, asks windows; flings boots into lake; Eve bruised by kiss; Brisson flees.
- Lepsius captured at St. Brieuc station; watch taken from Shan Healy. Lepsius imprisoned in tower chamber. Jeanne brings meals (disguised as man).
- Night: Shan Healy attempts rescue; blinded by vitriol thrown by Jeanne (Shan hit cheek and throat). Lepsius shoots Jeanne; bombs explode, château burns. Lepsius rescues Eve from fire; swims lake; yacht signals with cannon; Nundcumar picks them up; ship departs.

## CH XIV: AT SERAPIS
- Lepsius at Serapis (Brittany palace), with Nundcumar, Healy (sick, feverish), Hindoo servants. Eve kept in west ivory palace; sends note: "Lepsius, I admit myself your prisoner here..." Nundcumar's gossip: Pershorez (young poet), Barova (Arab slave-maid).
- Lepsius writes letters with riddles; Eve writes questions.
- Commissary Hugonnet searches Serapis; Lepsius hides Eve in secret room.
- Miss Ruth visits Serapis; Lepsius exchanges promises. Ruth finds Eve on west lake in gondola; sisters reunite.

## CH XV: TO SHUNTER
- Paris Moon-stock slumps; Lepsius's broker Monsieur Fautras; Schuré; Colonel Doumic; General Le Goffic; Saïd Pasha's Notes describe riots and Thiéry's speech. Thiéry offered portfolio; given two million francs bribe; Sauriau tempts him.
- Duc de Rey-Drouilhet poisons Thiéry's coffee with pills (after hesitation).
- Healy dies; Ruth reads Gethsemane passages. Nundcumar speaks last words.
- Lepsius blinded by vitriol in bath; dog Argo drugged; Jeanne hidden in coffer; attack. Lepsius and Eve; Eve's father; Jeanne on road claims Lepsius forgave her; Eve runs back to Lepsius.
- Lepsius ends praying at quay, Petit Bazaine; Eve says "Come."
